questions: Does the 6 cm sensor span lose the line on the tightest bends, and how often do line-loss events occur?
Is the signal stable with 12 mm footprints, or does it jitter when the tape crosses between sensors?
Is the 4 cm forward sensor offset useful, or does it make the controller react late or early?
Is wheel_track 0.12 m with radius 0.03 m too sluggish or too twitchy for the bend sharpness?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: Report whether the sensor layout or the drivetrain limits the controller more, and which of the two dimensions would you change first.

intent: Establish a balanced baseline: five forward-mounted sensors at 1.5 cm spacing, 12 mm footprints, and mid-range drivetrain and body values. Use the race to measure how this geometry behaves across the development tracks before narrowing any dimension.
learning: No prior evidence exists for this iteration. Build the next proposal from the rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation from this race together with the Integrator's report on which geometry limit they hit.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or integration feedback yet, so this is a baseline chosen for a line follower rather than one fitted to evidence. Five sensors spread across 6 cm of width give a clear centroid for the Integrator to work with while keeping the tape inside the sensor span on bends. The sensors sit 4 cm ahead of the axle so they see the line before the wheels reach it, which leaves time to correct steering. A 12 mm footprint is about half the 25 mm tape width, so a single sensor can read partial coverage and the signal varies smoothly as the line moves under it. Track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m are mid-range, giving a moderate turn authority and a speed capability well above the 1.5 m/s the course needs. Mass 0.8 kg and body width 0.12 m are moderate, and the 0.12 m width keeps the off-track limit at about 0.06 m. I expect this to complete the oval with few line losses. The main risks are weak response on tight slalom bends and sensor saturation on the widest turns, which the next race should show.
